ops_005:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare to create a 1Password Business account for our team password manager. This is a paid SaaS purchase requiring my explicit sign-off before anything is finalized, so your job is to prepare everything up to but not including the final purchase/contract acceptance.

Before starting, ask me for any of the following if not already known: our company/organization name to register, the admin email address to use for the account owner, the number of team seats we expect to need, and our preferred plan tier (e.g., Team or Business) if I have a preference.

Actions to take:
1. Navigate to the 1Password Business signup page.
2. Fill in the organization name, admin email, and plan selection using the details I provided.
3. Note the pricing, billing cadence (monthly/annual), and total estimated cost for the seat count I specified, so I can review before committing.
4. Do NOT enter any payment/billing card details, accept terms of service, or submit/finalize the purchase.
5. Prepare a short summary listing: the org name, admin email, plan selected, seat count, estimated cost, and a link to the terms of service for my review.

What done looks like: the signup form is filled out (or ready to fill) with confirmed values, and I have a clear summary with pricing and terms to review — but the account has not been created and no charge has been made.

Then stop for human sign-off. Report back to me with the prepared summary (org name, admin email, plan, seat count, cost estimate, terms link) and explicitly state that you are stopping for my approval before the purchase and contract acceptance proceed.

ops_005:n2.prompt:
You are helping me plan the creation of shared vaults in 1Password Business for our team's credential management. Do not create or modify any vaults yet — this step requires my explicit approval before any changes are applied.

First, ask me for any missing inputs: our company domain, our current team/department structure (e.g., Engineering, Marketing, Finance, IT, Ops), which employees or groups should have access to each department's credentials, and whether we need any cross-functional vaults (e.g., a company-wide 'Shared-IT' vault for tools everyone uses like WiFi or SaaS logins).

Using that information, draft a clear vault creation plan that includes: proposed vault names following a consistent naming convention, a short description of each vault's purpose, and the list of users or groups to be granted access to each vault (specify access level — e.g., read-only vs. manage). Also flag any vaults that should be restricted to admins only (e.g., a 'Break-glass/Admin' vault for critical shared credentials).

Present this plan to me in a clean, easy-to-review format (a table or numbered list is fine). Do not use my configured credentials to create anything in the 1Password admin console yet.

Once the plan is ready, stop for human sign-off. Report back with the full draft plan and a note confirming you have not made any changes, so I can review and approve before vault creation proceeds.

ops_005:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the 'invite team members' step of setting up 1Password Business as our team password manager. Do not actually send any invitations or apply any changes yet — a human must explicitly approve before anything is sent, per our process.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already provided: our 1Password Business account/team domain, the list of team members to invite (name, email address, intended role such as Administrator/Member, and which vault(s) or group(s) each person should have access to), and confirmation that I have admin access configured with my credentials.

Using your configured credentials, sign in to our 1Password Business admin console and review the current list of existing members and groups so we avoid duplicate invites or conflicting roles. Then prepare a clear, complete invite plan: for each person, list their email, proposed role, and the vault(s)/group(s) they'd be granted access to, matching any groupings we already use (e.g., Engineering, Finance, Ops). Flag any ambiguities — e.g., a person with no clear vault assignment, or a role that doesn't match our existing conventions — and propose a sensible default.

Present this invite plan to me as a numbered checklist, clearly labeled as a draft pending my approval. Do not submit or send invitations, and do not create groups or vaults, until I explicitly confirm. Once you've prepared the plan, stop for human sign-off.

When reporting back, give me: (1) the full draft invite list with roles and vault/group assignments, (2) any conflicts or ambiguities you found and how you resolved them or need my input, and (3) a clear statement that no invites have been sent and you are awaiting my approval to proceed.

ops_005:n4.prompt:
You are helping me configure access groups in our 1Password Business account for shared team credentials. Before starting, ask me for anything you need: our 1Password Business account/team name, the list of groups we want (e.g., Engineering, Finance, Marketing, IT Admins, Executives), which team members belong in each group, and which existing vaults or credential sets each group should ultimately have access to (this step only creates the groups; assigning vault permissions may be a separate step).

Using your configured credentials, sign in to our 1Password Business admin console and do the following:
1. Review current members and any existing groups so you don't create duplicates.
2. Draft a proposed set of access groups based on the roles/departments I gave you, including a short description of each group's purpose and the proposed member list.
3. Prepare the exact group names and membership lists in a clear checklist/table format, ready to be entered into the 1Password admin console.
4. Do NOT create or save any groups yet, and do not add or remove any members — this requires my explicit sign-off since a human must approve before changes are applied.

Once your draft is ready, present it to me as a summary: group name, description, and proposed members for each group. Flag any ambiguities (e.g., someone who could fit multiple groups, or a role with no clear group) for me to resolve.

After presenting the draft, stop for human sign-off. Do not create the groups, invite members, or apply any changes in 1Password until I explicitly approve the plan. Once I approve, wait for my confirmation before proceeding to actually create the groups in the admin console.
